name: Visa Exemption for Short-Term Stay
summary: Citizens of 74 countries and regions can enter Japan without a visa for short stays. Most get 90 days. Indonesia and Thailand get 15 days. Brunei and Qatar get 30 days.

other: Several countries need an ICAO-compliant ePassport (Malaysia, Thailand, Brazil, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Montenegro, Serbia, UAE).
Indonesia and Qatar must register their ePassport with a Japanese mission first.
Barbados, Turkiye and Lesotho need an ICAO-compliant machine-readable passport.
Taiwan: only passports with a personal ID number. Hong Kong: HKSAR passport or BNO passport with right of residence. Macao: Macao SAR passport only.
Austria, Germany, Ireland, Liechtenstein, Mexico, Switzerland and the UK can stay up to 6 months under bilateral arrangements, but must ask for an extension before day 90.
Uruguay passports issued after April 16, 2025 without a place of birth entry are not recognized.
The country list can change. Check the official list before booking.

stay.note: 15 days for Indonesia and Thailand, 30 days for Brunei and Qatar. Up to 6 months for a few countries with an extension.

name: JESTA (Japan Electronic System for Travel Authorization)
summary: Planned online pre-travel screening for visitors. It is announced but not open yet. The government is aiming to launch it within fiscal 2028.

other: Not open yet. Target launch is within fiscal 2028, moved up from fiscal 2030.
The official pages do not say exactly who it covers or what it costs. The fee is to be set with reference to other major countries.
Treat everything here as unconfirmed until the Immigration Services Agency publishes final rules.

sources.label: Immigration Services Agency: Early introduction of JESTA

name: JAPAN eVISA (tourism)
summary: Online single-entry tourist visa, up to 90 days, for ordinary passport holders who are residents of certain countries. Some countries must apply through an accredited agency.

other: Apply directly on the eVISA site if you are a resident of Australia, Brazil, Cambodia, Canada, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Taiwan, the UK or the USA (and not visa-exempt).

Through an accredited agency: residents of China, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Macau, Mongolia, South Korea, Singapore, UAE. Philippines and Viet Nam residents need a packaged tour by a designated agency.
Ordinary passports only. Travel must be by air or sea (scheduled ferries from Busan or Shanghai only).
You may be called for an interview. Show the visa issuance notice on a connected device at the airport. Screenshots and printouts are not accepted.

stay.note: China residents get 15 or 30 days. Viet Nam and Philippines nationals residing there get 15 days.

name: Short-Term Stay Visa (tourism, business, visiting family)
summary: Regular visa from a Japanese embassy or consulate for stays up to 90 days if your country is not visa-exempt. Business and similar trips can qualify for multiple-entry visas.

other: Documents vary by nationality. A letter of guarantee and invitation letters may be needed.
Colombian nationals are not on the visa-exempt list and need a visa in advance.
Check the embassy or consulate that covers your place of residence for the exact list.

processing: See the MOFA processing time page. Fees may vary by nationality and purpose, and nothing is charged if no visa is issued.

name: Transit through Japan
summary: Transit visa rules depend on your nationality. MOFA does not list them on its main visa pages, so check with the Japanese embassy or consulate that covers you.

other: No airside transit rule could be confirmed from an official page, so none is stated here.
Ask the Japanese embassy or consulate that covers your place of residence.

sources.label: MOFA: Visa overview and embassy contacts

name: Engineer / Specialist in Humanities / International Services
summary: The main work status for office and technical jobs with a Japanese employer. You need a degree or equivalent, or relevant experience, and a job that fits the category.

eligibility.education: University degree or equivalent. IT engineers can qualify with certain information technology exams.
other: Work needing foreign-culture thinking or sensitivity generally needs 3 years of related experience. University graduates in translation, interpreting or language teaching are exempt from that.
The job must fit natural science or humanities knowledge. Work covered by other statuses is excluded.
The official page states no salary threshold.

stay.note: Granted for 5 years, 3 years, 1 year or 3 months.

steps: Employer applies for a Certificate of Eligibility at a regional immigration office.
Apply for the visa at a Japanese embassy or consulate with the certificate.
Receive your residence card on arrival.

sources.label: Immigration Services Agency: Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services

name: Highly Skilled Professional (HSP) points system
summary: Points-based status for researchers, technical specialists and business managers. You need 70 points. It comes with a 5 year stay, looser work rules and a faster route to permanent residence.

other: 70 points needed. Points come from education, work experience, annual salary, age and Japanese ability, plus bonus points.
Categories: (i)(a) academic research, (i)(b) specialized and technical, (i)(c) business management.
For (i)(b) and (i)(c), an annual salary under 3 million yen disqualifies you whatever your points.
After 3 years as HSP (i) with 70+ points you can move to HSP (ii), which has no time limit.

sources.label: Immigration Services Agency: HSP points Q&A

name: Special Highly Skilled Professional (J-Skip)
summary: Fast lane for very high earners. If you meet the degree or experience and salary bar, you get HSP status without the points count.

income.note: Annual income threshold, not monthly. 20 million yen for research and technical roles, 40 million yen for business management.

other: Research or technical roles (HSP 1-a, 1-b): master's degree or higher, or 10+ years of experience, plus at least 20 million yen a year.
Business management (HSP 1-c): 5+ years of management experience and at least 40 million yen a year.
Income means expected pay from the planned activity in Japan.

name: Future Creation Individual (J-Find)
summary: Up to 2 years in Japan to job hunt or prepare a startup for graduates of top overseas universities.

savings.note: In your own name at the time of application.

eligibility.education: Degree from a university in the top 100 of at least two of QS, THE and ARWU rankings
other: Degree must have been awarded within the last 5 years.
A spouse or child can apply with proof of relationship.
The official university list is based on October 2026 rankings. Check the latest rankings when applying.

name: Business Manager
summary: Status for running or managing a business in Japan. Criteria got much stricter on October 16, 2025.

investment.note: Paid-in capital or total contributions for a company. Sole proprietors count total funds invested in the business.

eligibility.education: Master's, doctoral or professional degree in a relevant field, or 3+ years of business management experience
other: At least one full-time employee who is Japanese or holds a Table 2 status (permanent resident, spouse of Japanese, and similar).
The applicant or a full-time employee needs B2-level Japanese (for example JLPT N2).
A real office is required. A home office is generally not allowed.
The business plan must be reviewed by a certified management consultant, CPA or tax accountant in Japan.
Existing holders get until October 16, 2028 before renewals must meet the new criteria.

stay.note: Granted for 5 years, 3 years, 1 year, 4 months or 3 months.

sources.label: Immigration Services Agency: Revised Business Manager criteria
MOFA: Business Manager period of stay

name: Start-up Visa (Designated Activities)
summary: Six months to prepare a business in Japan with support from a local municipality. You then switch to Business Manager.

other: You must meet conditions set by a METI order and be supported by a municipality in Japan.
A Certificate of Eligibility is required. Spouse or child can apply without one.
Detailed criteria are on the METI site and were not confirmed here.

name: Specified Skilled Worker (i)
summary: Work status for labor-short industries. You pass a skills exam and a Japanese test (or finish technical intern training). Total stay is capped at 5 years.

eligibility.language: Japanese enough for daily life and work, shown by a Japanese test
other: Pass the skills exam for your industry field and the Japanese test. Technical intern completers are generally exempt.
Employer or a registered support organization must support you.
Family members generally cannot come along.
Cap on total stay is 5 years under this status. The list of industry fields changes, so check the current list.

stay.note: Renewed in blocks. Maximum 5 years in total.

sources.label: Immigration Services Agency: SSW system overview
Immigration Services Agency: Specified Skilled Worker status

name: Specified Skilled Worker (ii)
summary: Higher tier for workers with proficient skills in a smaller set of industry fields. It is renewable with no 5 year cap.

other: Work requiring skilled proficiency in an eligible industry field. Fewer fields are open than for SSW (i).
Detailed exam and experience requirements were not confirmed from official pages.

stay.note: Granted for 3 years, 2 years, 1 year or 6 months.

sources.label: Immigration Services Agency: Specified Skilled Worker status

name: Digital Nomad (Designated Activities)
summary: Up to 6 months in Japan working remotely for a foreign employer or your own overseas clients. No extension and no residence card.

income.note: Annual income at time of application, not monthly.

other: Only for citizens of visa-exempt countries that also have a tax convention with Japan.
Private medical travel insurance with at least 10 million yen coverage for injury and illness.
No employment contract with a Japanese organization. No work that requires being physically in Japan.
After the full 6 months you must wait 6 months before applying again.
Spouse and children can come on the same terms, with no income test of their own.

steps: Optional: get a Certificate of Eligibility from the immigration office.
Apply at the Japanese embassy or consulate with income proof, insurance proof and an activity plan.
Enter Japan. No residence card is issued.
documents: Proof of annual income of 10 million yen or more

name: Long-Stay Sightseeing and Recreation (Designated Activities)
summary: Six months for wealthy visitors from visa-exempt countries, extendable to one year once.

savings.note: Savings equivalent to more than 30 million yen. If a spouse stays separately, combined savings must exceed 60 million yen.

other: Nationals of visa-waiver countries or regions only.
A spouse can come along. Dependent children cannot.
Extend once, before the 6 months run out, to a maximum of 1 year.

stay.note: Extendable once to a total of 1 year.

name: Student
summary: Status for studying at a Japanese university, vocational school or language school. Part-time work is allowed with permission.

other: A Certificate of Eligibility from a regional immigration office is normal. You can apply without one but it needs many more documents and can take months.
Documents include a graduation certificate and proof of the financial supporter's employment.
Language school applicants now need a Japanese test certificate or a school interview (applies to students enrolling from October 2026).
The government is tightening oversight of student work and schools.

stay.note: Up to 4 years and 3 months per grant, set individually.

sources.label: Immigration Services Agency: Part-time work permission for students
Immigration Services Agency: Japanese language school entry changes

name: Spouse or Child of Japanese National
summary: Family status for spouses and children of Japanese citizens. It carries no restrictions on work.

other: Apply with a Certificate of Eligibility, usually filed in Japan by the Japanese spouse.
Full eligibility criteria are not spelled out on the MOFA page.

stay.note: Granted for 5 years, 3 years, 1 year or 6 months.

sources.label: MOFA: Spouse or Child of Japanese National
Immigration Services Agency: Guide to residence procedures

name: Spouse of Permanent Resident
summary: Status for the spouse of a permanent resident. MOFA lists it for spouses only.

other: Eligibility criteria are not spelled out on the MOFA page.
Apply with a Certificate of Eligibility.

stay.note: Granted for 5 years, 3 years, 1 year or 6 months.

name: Dependent (Family Stay)
summary: Status for family members supported by someone on certain work or study statuses. Work is generally not allowed without extra permission.

other: The MOFA page does not state who qualifies.
Dependents are generally not allowed to work without permission to engage in other activities.
Apply with a Certificate of Eligibility.

sources.label: Immigration Services Agency: Guide to residence procedures

name: Working Holiday
summary: A holiday visa that lets young people from partner countries work on the side to fund their trip. 33 partner countries and regions.

other: Age limit is 25 for Australia, Canada and South Korea unless the two countries agree to extend it to 30.
You must live in your country of nationality when applying.
No dependents or children can come along.
You need a return ticket or funds to buy one, plus reasonable funds for the first stay, and good health.
Work at bars, cabarets, nightclubs and gambling places is not allowed.
Most nationals can only use it once. A few (including Canada, UK, New Zealand, Denmark, Austria, Germany, Ireland, Slovakia, South Korea, Taiwan) can do it a second time.
Apply at the Japanese embassy or consulate in your country. Taiwan applicants use the Japan-Taiwan Exchange Association.

name: Long-Term Resident (Teijusha)
summary: A status the Minister of Justice grants individually, for example to refugees and people recognized for complementary protection. It has no work restrictions.

other: Granted case by case. Criteria were not read in detail here.
Refugees and complementary protection recipients are generally granted this status.
Descendants of Japanese emigrants can also use it. See the Immigration Services Agency guide for fourth-generation Japanese descendants.

sources.label: Immigration Services Agency: Guide to residence procedures
Immigration Services Agency: Guide for fourth-generation Japanese descendants

name: Permanent Residence (standard route)
summary: In principle you need 10 years of continuous residence, with at least 5 of those on a work or residence status. Rules are being tightened from April 1, 2027.

eligibility.language: About B1 Japanese under the Japanese Language Education Framework, with exceptions
other: Good conduct, with a clean record on laws and immigration duties.
Household income above the Japanese average for your household size, plus pension and savings checks.
Taxes, public health insurance and public pension must be paid. Past delinquency counts against you.
You should hold the longest period of stay available to you.
In the 10 years before applying, one absence of 6 months or more, or 2 years 6 months in total, is generally viewed negatively.
School-age children should attend Japanese schools.
The revised guideline (Oct 1, 2026) applies to applications filed from April 1, 2027. The law will also add grounds to revoke permanent residence.

stay.note: Permanent residence has no expiry, but the card must be renewed.

sources.label: Immigration Services Agency: Permanent Residence Guidelines (revised Oct 1, 2026)
Immigration Services Agency: Government response on permanent residence

name: Permanent Residence (Highly Skilled Professional fast track)
summary: HSP holders with 70 points can apply after 3 years. With 80 points it is 1 year. J-Skip holders can apply after 1 year.

other: 70+ points: 3 years of continuous residence, either keeping 70 points for 3 years, or having had 70 points 3 years before applying.
80+ points: 1 year, under the same two ways of counting.
Special Highly Skilled Professional (J-Skip): 1 year.
HSP holders and their families are exempt from the B1 Japanese requirement under the revised guideline.
Business manager applicants must meet the new Business Manager criteria.

sources.label: Immigration Services Agency: Permanent Residence Guidelines (revised Oct 1, 2026)
Immigration Services Agency: HSP points Q&A

name: Permanent Residence (spouse or child of a Japanese national)
summary: A shorter route for spouses and children of Japanese citizens. Official sources differ on the exact years, so confirm before relying on it.

other: Older Immigration Services Agency material says 1 year of residence plus 3 years of marriage for spouses.
The revised guideline (Oct 1, 2026) says a real marriage of at least 5 years with at least 3 years of continuous residence in Japan, and 3 years of residence for children of a Japanese national.
The revised guideline applies to applications filed from April 1, 2027.
Good conduct and independent livelihood requirements are waived for these applicants.

sources.label: Immigration Services Agency: Permanent Residence Guidelines (revised Oct 1, 2026)
Immigration Services Agency: Government response on permanent residence

name: Naturalization
summary: The law requires 5 years of continuous residence. Since April 1, 2026 the Ministry of Justice looks for about 10 years and proof you fit into Japanese society. Japan generally does not allow dual citizenship.

eligibility.language: Enough Japanese for daily life: speaking, reading and writing. No fixed test is stated.
other: At least 5 years of continuous residence with valid status (Nationality Act).
Per the Justice Minister (March 27, 2026), in principle 10 years or more plus integration into Japanese society, with a longer check of tax and social insurance payments.
Upright conduct and ability to support yourself, judged at the household level.
You generally must give up your other nationality, unless you cannot renounce it.
Conditions are eased for people with special ties, such as Japanese spouses, children of Japanese nationals, and people born in Japan.
Approval is not guaranteed. Apply in person at a Legal Affairs Bureau.

citizenship.note: Statutory minimum is 5 years. Practice moved toward 10 years from April 1, 2026. Applicants generally must lose their other nationality.

sources.label: Ministry of Justice: Minister press conference, Mar 27, 2026

name: Citizenship by Descent or Birth
summary: A child is Japanese if a parent is Japanese at birth. Birth in Japan alone does not give citizenship, except for a child of unknown or stateless parents.

other: A child born abroad to a Japanese parent who also gets a foreign nationality must have a parent notify the intent to keep Japanese nationality within 3 months of birth, or it is lost retroactively.
Dual nationals must choose one nationality. Those who became dual before 18 choose by age 20. Those who became dual at 18 or older choose within 2 years.
A child recognized by a Japanese father after birth may get nationality by notification if requirements are met.

citizenship.note: Dual nationality is tolerated only until the choice deadline. After that you must pick one.
